beats.care: It shows no T20 total is safe anymore. India's bowlers will be under real pressure in the next match of the series.
beats.what: India made 249 for 5 in the second T20 international in Ranchi. West Indies chased it down with nine balls left.
beats.why: Captain Shai Hope hit an unbeaten 102 off 45 balls, and Sherfane Rutherford smashed 84 off 37 after West Indies were 5 for 2.

cards.body: Sanju Samson's 82 off 41 powered India to 249/5. Mayank Yadav's early burst left West Indies at 5/2, and it looked over. Then Hope and Rutherford added 120 for the fourth wicket, and WI got home in 18.3 overs. Lowkey one of the wildest T20Is this year.
That partnership turned a wobbly chase into a cruise.
cards.caption: Hope and Rutherford's 4th-wicket stand

cards.body: The record chase is still South Africa's 259/4 at Centurion in 2023. The team they beat? West Indies.

cards.q: 250 chased with 9 balls left. Is T20 now too batting-friendly?

opts: A 120-run stand between Hope and Rutherford
cards.q: What turned the chase for West Indies?
cards.why: After slipping to 5 for 2, Hope and Rutherford's huge partnership swung the game West Indies' way.

cover.label: West Indies' winning chase in Ranchi

hook: India scored *249* and still lost. How did West Indies pull it off?
